newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firm, tone improving.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firm, tone improving.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended firm Wednesday, on moderate volumes, with sentiment seen improving after 12 days of consolidation near the year's lows.
"Precious metals look like they forming a base around current levels, with spot silver closing today right on its 50-day moving average," Mitsui & Co USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
"The gains today in platinum also helped and may make the shorts nervous, while producer selling has been very limited recently."
COMEX February gold closed up 80 cents at $371.30 an ounce, on total estimated volume of 20,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $369.10/369.60, against the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $368.70, and up from the New York close Tuesday at $368.40/368.80.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell 3,507 ounces to 742,348 ounces Tuesday and remain near 19 year lows.
The decline in near term gold implied lease rates in the past few days also suggested some easing up in speculative short positions, traders said.
"The gold market has been dominated by two trends in late 1996 - a lack of physical investment demand and heavy short selling in the futures and options markets," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"These trends may continue for a while yet, although the short selling appears to have approached, if not reached, its ultimate end," he said.
"As a result prices may rise a bit in late 1996 and early 1997 and should the equity values plateau at this time, the rebound may be more powerful."
March silver ended unchanged at $4.893 an ounce, after trading up to a 15 day intraday high at $4.955 Tuesday.
COMEX warehouse silver stocks rose 535,838 ounces to 144,191,631 ounces Tuesday, but Wilmington Trust stocks fell 621,679 ounces to 57,639,217 ounces in the week ended December 18.
Wilmington Trust in Delaware becomes an official exchange silver depositary from January 1, 1997.
NYMEX January platinum ended up $3.10 an ounce at $374.90, an eight day high, with the April platinum/gold spread jumping to $3.40 an ounce from 70 cents Tuesday.
"Russian platinum exports held up relatively high in 1996, but may fall in 1997," Kempf said.
NYMEX March palladium was up $1.80 cents to $121.25.

Russian palladium exports may also decline in 1997, but whether or not this happens may depend more on Russian financial conditions than on conditions in the Russian nickel and PGM (platinum group metals) producing industries," he said.
